question: Should `contextPruning.ttl` remain a tool-result-only prompt-cache optimization, or should OpenClaw add or retarget an authorized session/context pruning contract for normal conversation history?
rationale: Current code and docs intentionally preserve full transcripts while pruning only in-memory tool results, so changing TTL semantics or adding mutation endpoints needs product and security intent.

options.title: Define explicit session/context contract
options.body: Add a typed admin-gated prune/reset/compact design with clear transcript persistence, summarization, audit, and integration semantics.

options.title: Clarify current TTL semantics
options.body: Document that TTL does not expire normal conversation history and split remaining needs across the existing REST controls, rolling pruning, manual tool clearing, and session rotation issues.

options.title: Retarget TTL to conversation history
options.body: Change `contextPruning.ttl` semantics only with upgrade notes, tests, and security review for persisted history and memory summarization behavior.

recommendation.title: Define explicit session/context contract
recommendation.body: Add a typed admin-gated prune/reset/compact design with clear transcript persistence, summarization, audit, and integration semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the latest maintainer review on this issue and recent history on the cache-ttl/session-pruning surface.
